When the channel executed a row, from the row's own log

report_executions.Rd

The date of activation is the channel's first write of applied_seal, and not outcome_at: the outcome is rewritten at every outcome, so a row that went from applied to transport_error and back would look activated twice. Only the round writes the seal, and only when it has applied the row; a row executed again after an approved change writes a new one, which is how the report tells a modified request from a new one.

Usage

report_executions(events, record, channel_account = NULL)

Arguments

events

The event log, as register_log() returns it.

record

The record id.

channel_account

The REDCap usernames that hold the register's token, one or more, or NULL when they are not configured, for log_channel_accounts().

Value

The stamps of the channel's seal writes, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M" in Rome, oldest first; character() when there is none; NA_character_ when the log cannot say.

Details

The events are filtered here by record, whatever REDCap did with the parameter. Measured on 2026-10-16 that exportLogging honors it; the filter stays, at no cost, because an instance that ignored it would hand back the whole log, where another row's execution would date this one.

The author has to be the channel, the account log_channel_accounts() names: the configured channel_account, or, without it, whoever wrote the channel's fields. With the account configured, a write of the seal by any other account executed nothing and is ignored, a referent's import included. Without it, when two accounts write those fields the log cannot say which of them executed the row, log_channel_unknown(), and the answer is unknown rather than a guess.

Only the row that stands now is read. The register reuses record ids: one made for a field test, deleted on 2026-09-01 with the rest and made again as a real request, has both lives in its log, and the old one's seal would date the new request months before it existed, and make its first execution read as a change. log_of_record() keeps the row's current life only, from its newest creation on, as for the round, and the channel's account is recognized on that.

The stamps stay in the instance's civil time, which is Rome: measured on 2026-09-01, a round at 21:03 UTC is logged at 23:03, and again on 2026-10-16, a first seal logged at 22:04 beside an outcome_at of 20:03 UTC. A month is then the first seven characters of the stamp, and no conversion can shift a row activated on the last evening of the month into the next one.
